cells.tense: Right now the knowing runs full and holds several true readings at once without dropping any.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Before a conversation drifts, name the shape first — one sentence saying what this is and what it isn't. No case stacked after it. Let that sentence stand where all of you can see it.
cells.core:
You can carry several true readings at once and not force them to agree yet. When something that couldn't hold comes down near you, you don't grab the nearest story that fits; what's left standing is clean. And the people with you go steadier, because they can tell the ground isn't going anywhere. That steadiness isn't a pose you put on.

You've known this shape for a while and kept it in your head, where it does less than you think. This week, say it out loud before anyone asks. One sentence, to whoever is there, no argument behind it. Nobody has to sign on. What you'll notice is how much of what came down came down quietly, while the shape stayed a private possession.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold many versions and keep your footing.
cells.verb: Holding many true things at once
cells.place: In the clearing where a structure that couldn't hold has just come down

cells.tense: Running ahead of the next collapse, bracing for structures that have not fallen yet.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: For three days, aim at a single heading and leave the others unexamined on purpose — one project, one choice, one person. Let your whole line of sight rest there and skip the audit till day four.
cells.core:
You've had the shape of things for a while, and now you keep arriving ahead of it — spotting the cracked premise three moves out and pulling it down before anyone else has noticed the crack. It looks like foresight. From inside, it's a survey you can't switch off, and it buys no safety: whatever's coming comes whether or not you pre-cleared the room for it. The watching has become the work.

This week, aim at one heading and leave the others alone on purpose. Not the one with the best argument — the one you'd actually move toward. Three days is enough to find out. If the other directions pull at you, check them on day four. Notice what goes quiet in you once every possibility isn't being held open at once, and whether anything was actually being held by the watching.

cells.tense: Standing at a door that has already shut, still describing what was on the far side.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Say the picture aloud to someone — not your conclusion, the thing as it actually looks to you. No hedging, no defense, no fixing it if they shrug. Let them hold it with you a few minutes.
cells.core:
You can still see it. Whatever you read off a room, you read it fast and accurately, and lately almost none of it leaves your head. It arrives, gets weighed, and stays. Nothing goes back out. You've been treating that as a fact about the world — nobody asks, nothing to say — which is one way to describe it and not the only way.

Say the picture to one person. Not the conclusion you've built from it; the thing as it actually appears when you look. Plainly, without bracing for their reaction, without adjusting it after they answer. They can hold it for a while. You'll find out from inside whether the reason you stopped saying things aloud is still running.

cells.tense: Doing the reading and then handing the credit to the situation, calling it plain sense.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: When a small case turns on your read, back your read out loud once — a sentence, no proof, then let it stand. Watch where the credit goes and don't correct the room.
cells.core:
You read situations, and you act on the read, and the doing gets filed under something else — being practical, noticing what was already obvious, saying what anyone would have said. You'll hold four or five readings of a thing at once and then tell the room it saw the same. The compass that picked is the one thing about you that stays out of the account.

When a small case turns on your read, back your read out loud once — one sentence, no chain of proof behind it — and don't unfold the rest if someone pushes back. Pushback can stay theirs. You'll want to lay out every step that got you there. Don't. Do the small thing the compass says, then leave the credit where the room puts it and see how that sits.
cells.sheetLine: You see it, and the credit goes to the situation.
cells.verb: Holding many true things at once
cells.place: In the clearing where a structure that couldn't hold has just come down

attempts.check: The unsupported claim I am tempted to make is that the person has recently stopped trusting their own perceptions because a structure fell — the record gives the capacity and the season of clearing, not the history. A reader could reasonably say the collapse was loss, not liberation, and that nothing about their situation was false. The asks survive that: assertion, orientation, merge and conscience are all useful whether the read lands or not. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you know the truth and others don't,' which flatters the reader instead of equipping them.
